notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix (none found for the phrase order at 85). §1985:IX.4.9.2 prints WRITE record-name-1 [ FROM identifier-1 ] [ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1 ] [ NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-2 ] [ END-WRITE ]. The superset rule writeStatement accepts it, SequentialIoBinder.BindWrite resolves record-name-1 and routes an indexed file to KeyedIoBinder.BindWrite, which refuses the sequential format's ADVANCING and END-OF-PAGE phrases on it (COBOL1720; INVALID KEY beside ADVANCING is COBOL2269 from the WRITE row of ConditionalPhraseAssociation.Owners). The later formats' additions are refused at --std 85: FROM literal-1 and FROM a figurative constant by VisitRecordFromPhrase (COBOL0871), FILE file-name-1 by DeclinedFilePhrase (COBOL1706), RETRY by VisitRetryPhrase and WITH [NO] LOCK by VisitRecordLockPhrase (COBOL0900); the word RECORD after record-name-1, an AT END phrase and FROM after the phrases are syntax errors. All probed at 85. What is NOT implemented is the printed sequence of the two phrases: the conditionalPhrases loop and ConditionalPhraseAssociation.Associates / MayAssociate have no edition arm for the order, so NOT INVALID KEY before INVALID KEY compiles at 85; either order is the 2002 change §2002:F.2 item 33 ("The conditional phrases in the ... WRITE statements may be specified in any order"), which the row's change record names. Same mechanism as the DELETE, READ, REWRITE and START rows of this slice. The witness runs WRITE ... FROM with both phrases in the printed order and END-WRITE, a new key and a duplicate.

next.reason: 1985: "WRITE record-name-1 [FROM identifier-1] [INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1] [NOT INVALID KEY ...]"; 2023: "WRITE {record-name-1|FILE file-name-1} [FROM {identifier-1|literal-1}] [retry-phrase] [WITH LOCK|WITH NO LOCK]". 2023 Format 2 (indexed/relative) adds the FILE phrase, a FROM literal, RETRY and LOCK phrases. Choice indicators let INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY appear in either order.
